---
title: "4. Data Import & Export"
description: "Reading and Writing Data: The `libname` equivalent."
---

# Reading SAS Data

The `haven` package is the gold standard for reading `.sas7bdat` and `.xpt` files.

```r
library(haven)
library(here)

# Reading a SAS dataset
# equivalent to: set mylib.adae;
adae <- read_sas(here("data", "adae.sas7bdat"))

# Reading an XPT file (common for FDA submissions)
dm_xpt <- read_xpt(here("data", "dm.xpt"))
```

## Handling Labels and Formats

`haven` imports SAS labels as an attribute called `label`.
It imports SAS formats as `format`.

You can view these with:
```r
# View variable label
attr(adae$AESEV, "label")
```

# Reading CSVs and Excel

Use `readr` (part of tidyverse) for CSVs and `readxl` for Excel.

```r
library(readr)
library(readxl)

# PROC IMPORT (CSV)
labs <- read_csv(here("data", "labs.csv"))

# PROC IMPORT (Excel)
# You can specify the sheet
codes <- read_excel(here("data", "codelist.xlsx"), sheet = "AESOC")
```

# Writing Data

Just as you read, you can write.

```r
# Export to SAS
write_sas(adae, here("output", "adae_new.sas7bdat"))

# Export to CSV
write_csv(labs, here("output", "labs_clean.csv"))
```

# Saving R Objects (`.rds`)

If you are working strictly within R, save your files as `.rds`. It preserves all R-specific attributes (factors, classes) perfectly and is compressed.

```r
# Save single object
write_rds(adae, here("data", "adae.rds"))

# Read it back
adae <- read_rds(here("data", "adae.rds"))
```
